title: Initialization of the schedule configuration
statement: Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a,v\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a word of schedule symbols, and choose a base configuration on $x$, a valid input-head position $p$, and a bit word $w$ whose little-endian value is $v$. Assume $|x|+1\le (a+1)(v+1)$. Then there is a bit word $w'$ of the same length as $w$ such that, after exactly $(p-1+2)+(2|x|+4)+(v+1)(2|w|+(a+1)+4)+14(a+1)(v+1)+10$ steps from the reset-start setup with budget head at $|w|+1$, unary head at $1$ over the empty unary counter, and blank guide, the machine is in the macrostep-check phase with input head at $|x|+1$, budget head at $|w|+1$ over the captured clock tape for $w'$, unary head at $1$ over the unary tape with $(a+1)(v+1)$ markers, and guide head at $0$ over the guide of radius $3(a+1)(v+1)$.
hypotheses_covered: W is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
a and v are natural numbers
base is a configuration on x
p is a valid input-head position
the little-endian value of w equals v
replaced:
Let $w$ be a bit word of little-endian value $v$, and suppose the input satisfies
$|x| + 1 \le (a+1)(v+1)$, where $a$ is the padding parameter.  Consider a setup
configuration in the reset-start phase with input head at an arbitrary position $p$,
budget head at cell $|w|+1$ over the captured clock tape of $w$, unary head at cell $1$
over the unary tape with zero markers, and guide head at cell $0$ over the blank guide
tape.  Then there is a bit word $w'$ with $|w'| = |w|$ such that after exactly
\[
  \bigl(\max(p,1)+1\bigr) + \bigl(2|x| + 4\bigr)
  + (v+1)\bigl(2|w| + (a+1) + 4\bigr) + \bigl(14\,(a+1)(v+1) + 10\bigr)
\]
steps the machine is in the macrostep-check phase with input head parked at position
$|x|+1$, budget head at cell $|w|+1$ over the captured clock tape of $w'$, unary head
at cell $1$ over the unary tape with $(a+1)(v+1)$ markers, and guide head at cell $0$
over the completed guide of radius $3\,(a+1)(v+1)$: the binary counter retains its full
width throughout.
